# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: SCS character sets, shifts and DECNRCM  (issue #112, wave 9)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/charset_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output)
#
# Same machine-readable layout as csi_spec.txt / decstr_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note /
# screen / cursor / pending_wrap / requests / scrollback), parsed by tests/spec/mod.rs. Extra keys the
# shared parser ignores: flags (xterm-quirk | decision | control | level) and, on a `decision` row that deviates
# from xterm, xterm_screen (what xterm shows instead; documentation only). `control` rows run a
# stream without the reset or save the neighbouring row tests (proof the setup is not vacuous);
# `level` rows start with a DECSCL (61 = VT100, 65 = VT500); `decision` rows encode a choice between sources.
# Cursor is 0-based (row,col). render_screen puts `|` AFTER the cursor's cell; a row ending in `\`
# is soft-wrapped. Non-ASCII payload is written as \u{..}; expected screens are literal characters.
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (all fetched and read for this fixture; tags used in the cite: lines)
#   [CTL]   xterm ctlseqs  https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html
#           "ESC ( C Designate G0 Character Set" (and ) * + - . /), "ESC n/o/|/}/~", "ESC N/O", SI/SO,
#           "CSI ? 42 h/l DECNRCM", DA1 "Ps = 9 National Replacement Character sets".
#   [XT-cs] xterm charsets.c  xtermCharSetOut() (the print-time translation) and HandleUPSS/isSevenBit
#           https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/charsets.c  (rev 1.131, 2026-04)
#   [XT-tbl] xterm charsets.h  the map_NRCS_*, map_DEC_Technical, map_DEC_Supp_Graphic tables
#   [XT-cp] xterm charproc.c  select_charset(), scs_table[], xtermDecodeSCS(), resetCharsets(),
#           CASE_SO/SI/SS2/SS3/LS2/LS3/LS1R/LS2R/LS3R, WriteNow(), dotext(), modified_DECNRCM(),
#           ReallyReset() (RIS, DECSTR, DECSCL), srm_DECNRCM, CASE_GSETS*/CASE_SCS*
#   [XT-vt] xterm VTPrsTbl.c  scstable / scs96table / scs_pct_table / scs_amp_table / scs_2qt_table
#           (which finals dispatch to which CASE_GSETS*)
#   [XT-cu] xterm cursor.c  CursorSave2() / CursorRestoreFlags(): the saved cursor holds curgl, curgr, gsets[]
#   [XT-fu] xterm fontutils.c  dec2ucs(): the DEC Special Graphics to Unicode table
#   [VT510] VT510 Programmer Reference  https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/SCS.html, DECNRCM.html, DECSTR.html
#   [VTTEST] vttest 20251205 charsets.c  (KnownCharsets[]: which sets are NRCS-only, which levels)
#   [TERMINFO] `infocmp -1 xterm-256color`: smacs=\E(0, rmacs=\E(B, sgr0=\E(B\E[m, rs2=\E[!p\E[?3;4l\E[4l\E>
#   esctest2 (ThomasDickey/esctest2): has NO test for SCS, SO, SI or the shifts (see "ISSUE-TEXT ERRORS");
#           it covers DECRC without a save (save_restore_cursor.py), the alt-screen saved cursor
#           (test_SaveRestoreCursor_AltVsMain) and lists G0-G3/GL/GR in decstr.py's DECSTR table.
#
# HOW xterm TRANSLATES IN UTF-8 MODE (the oracle for every row; Tessera is always UTF-8)
#   1. print time, per character (charsets.c xtermCharSetOut): skipped entirely when GL (or the single-
#      shifted set) and GR are both ASCII. Otherwise, for a code point c <= 0xFF:
#        cs    = (c >= 0x80) ? gsets[curgr] : gsets[curgl or curss];      seven = c & 0x7f
#        chr   = set-specific map of `seven` (or of c for ASCII, the supplementals' default, British w/o NRC)
#        drop  if chr == 0x7f and cs is a seven-bit set (DEL)
#        if c >= 0x80 and 0x20 < chr < 0x80: chr |= 0x80
#      Code points above 0xFF are never translated. So GL translates ASCII, GR translates U+0080..U+00FF.
#   2. designation (charproc.c): the final byte is looked up in scs_table[] with the DECSCL level and
#      DECNRCM; no row => G-set := ASCII ("unknown GSET"), but finals that never reach the lookup
#      (ground-state finals, level-5 prefixes below level 5, level-1 non-VT100 finals) leave it alone.
#   3. default sets in UTF-8: G0..G3 = ASCII, GL = G0, GR = G2 (resetCharsets, dft_upss = ASCII).
#      Designating G2 therefore changes what GR does at once.
#
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommended option first; all are rows with flags: decision)
#   D-BRITISH  xterm's UK set (`ESC ( A`) maps # to the pound sign only with DECNRCM on or at level 1; at the
#              default level 4 without DECNRCM it prints #. Every other terminal maps always. vttest lists
#              British as an NRCS (tested only with DECNRCM on). Recommend xterm (row NR9C), document it.
#   D-SS       xterm keeps a pending single shift across controls and other escapes until a printable arrives
#              (row SS06). Recommend xterm.
#   D-NRCM-OFF DECRST 42 keeps the designated national sets (row NR93); DEC says they need national mode.
#   D-DECSTR   DECSTR keeps DECNRCM in xterm (row NR95); DEC table 5-9 resets it. Recommend xterm.
#   D-UTF8-NRC xterm's modified_DECNRCM flips the UTF-8 decoder off while DECNRCM is on (bytes are then
#              Latin-1/8-bit and GR sees raw bytes). Tessera keeps decoding UTF-8 and applies the NRCS tables
#              to the decoded code points (so Dutch ij, florin and the other UNI() entries always map).
#              Not testable through a byte stream; documented here and in ADR 0033.
#   D-LEVELS   Sets that xterm offers only at level 5 (Greek, Hebrew, Turkish, Russian, Cyrillic, SCS NRCS,
#              the ISO Latin-2/5/Greek/Hebrew/Cyrillic 96-sets) and the level-3-only JIS sets are not
#              implemented: they behave as xterm does at level 4 (rows SU08..SU11, SG10). DECSCL 65 does not
#              enable them. Recommend a follow-up issue if anyone needs them.
#
# ISSUE-TEXT ERRORS / NOTES
#   * "esctest decscs/so/si pending cases": esctest2 has none (no scs.py, so.py or si.py) and
#     esctest_pending.txt has no block. The runnable pieces are the vttest menu 2 screen 15 row
#     (csi_spec.txt, V2S15) and the DECRC / alt-screen / DECSTR cases cited above.
#   * "DECSTR and RIS reset G0-G3 = ASCII, GL = G0, GR = G2": right for xterm in UTF-8 mode. In an 8-bit
#     xterm the default G2/G3 would be DEC Supplemental (UPSS), not ASCII (resetCharsets comment).
#   * "ESC - . / 96-char designations ... if xterm supports them at level 4": only ESC - / . / with final A
#     (ISO Latin-1 Supplemental) works at level 4; B F H L M are level 5 (rows SU05..SU10).
#   * DEC Supplemental `ESC ( <` is level 2 only; from level 3 the same final is the user-preferred set
#     (UPSS), which in xterm's UTF-8 mode is ISO Latin-1 (identity without DECNRCM): row SU04.
#   * DA1 feature 9 (NRCS) and DECRQM ?42 replies are checked in reports_spec.txt, not here.
# =============================================================================


### SG01_dec_special_all_of_0x5f_to_0x7e
size: 3x40
step: feed \x1b(0_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~
cite: [XT-cs] xtermCharSetOut case nrc_DEC_Spec_Graphic (seven > 0x5f && <= 0x7e -> dec2ucs(seven-0x5f); 0x5f -> 0); [XT-fu] fontutils.c dec2ucs table; [VT510] SCS "0" DEC Special Graphic
note: All 32 codes 0x5f..0x7e through G0=DEC Special Graphics. 0x5f maps to a blank (xterm stores code 0; Tessera shows a space, kitty and VTE do the same). 0x60..0x7e are the Unicode box-drawing and symbol characters xterm uses in UTF-8 mode.
screen:
> ◆▒␉␌␍␊°±␤␋┘┐┌└┼⎺⎻─⎼⎽├┤┴┬│≤≥π≠£· |
>
>
cursor: (0,32)
pending_wrap: false

### SG02_dec_special_leaves_other_ascii
size: 3x100
step: feed \x1b(0 !"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^
cite: [XT-cs] xtermCharSetOut: `else { chr = seven; }` for the DEC Special Graphic case outside 0x5f..0x7e
note: Space through ^ (0x20..0x5e) are not remapped; digits, capitals and punctuation print as ASCII.

### SS10_ss_with_the_default_gr_is_g2
size: 3x40
step: feed \x1b*0\x1bN\u{ec}
cite: [XT-cs] xtermCharSetOut: eight >= 128 -> rightset = gsets[curgr] (G2 by default)
note: A Latin-1 code point uses GR (gsets[curgr]), not the single-shifted set; GR defaults to G2, so here both are the special set.
screen:
>┌ |
>
>
cursor: (0,1)

### GR14_unmapped_gr_codes_get_bit_7_back
size: 3x40
step: feed \x1b)0\x1b~\u{df}\u{c1}
flags: xterm-quirk
cite: [XT-cs] xtermCharSetOut: `if (eight >= 128 && chr < 128 && chr > 32) chr |= 128` after the DEC Special Graphic case left chr = seven
note: U+00DF (seven 0x5F) and U+00C1 (seven 0x41) are not in the line-drawing range, so xterm folds them to seven bits and sets bit 7 again: both print as themselves. Without the fix-up they would print as _ and A.
